The bilateral agreement remains in force for a period of **five (5) years** and is **renewed for a similar period** unless one party officially notifies the other, through diplomatic channels, of its desire to suspend or terminate the agreement. In that case, the agreement remains valid until sixty (60) days after the notification. [Source 1: Philippines‑Saudi Arabia Bilateral Agreement on Domestic Worker Recruitment (2013).pdf, page 4]

An OWWA membership stays active until the expiration of the OFW’s existing employment contract or after two (2) years from the contract effectivity, whichever comes first. This is stated in RA 10801 (Sec. 9) and reiterated in the OWWA Citizens Charter (2026, 1st Edition), page 19.

No.  Under Republic Act 11862, cases involving trafficking in persons **shall not be dismissed** based on an Affidavit of Desistance executed by the victim or their parents or legal guardians. Public and private prosecutors are directed to oppose and manifest objections to motions for dismissal, and any attempt to unduly pressure the complainant to execute such an affidavit is punishable. [RA_11862_relevant_excerpts.pdf, page 3]

The penalty for committing any act of trafficking in persons as defined in Section 4 (as amended by RA 10364) is:

- **Imprisonment of twenty (20) years**  
- **A fine of not less than One million pesos (P1,000,000.00) but not more than Two million pesos (P2,000,000.00)**  

This is stated in RA 10364, Sec. 12, which amends Sec. 10 of R.A. 9208. [RA_10364_relevant_excerpts.pdf, p2]
The 2022 IRR of the anti‑trafficking law allows you to report suspected trafficking through the **IACAT 1343 Action Line**【Source 1: Anti‑Trafficking_IRR_2022_relevant_excerpts.pdf, page 2】.

A licensed recruitment agency that wants to get accreditation of a direct employer on a per‑employer basis must submit the following documents:

1. Verified Special Power of Attorney (SPA) issued by the direct employer in favor of the Philippine recruitment agency indicating the name of the worker, salary and other benefits.  
2. Verified employment contract duly accomplished by the parties concerned.  
3. Visa or its equivalent document.  
4. Full and complete assumption of responsibility of the Philippine licensed agency over its deployed household workers.  
5. Medical result showing fitness of the household workers.  
6. Certificate of Attendance to Pre‑Departure Orientation Seminar (PDOS).  

These requirements are listed in **POEA_MC19_1999_SupplementaryGuidelines_KSA.txt**.
The OWWA membership contribution under RA 10801 is **US$ 25.00** (or its equivalent in the prevailing foreign exchange rates)【RA 10801.txt】.
Ang mga overseas offices ng Department of Migrant Workers ay tinatawag na **Migrant Workers Office (MWO)**. [Source 4]

RA 10022 (the Labor Code amendment) imposes the following penalty for illegal recruitment: imprisonment of **not less than twelve (12) years and one (1) day but not more than twenty (20) years** and a fine of **not less than One million pesos (P1,000,000.00) nor more than Two million pesos (P2,000,000.00)**.  
[RA10022_Amendment_2010.txt]

Under the **Migrant Workers Act (RA 8042)**, illegal recruitment carries **life imprisonment** when the offense is **classified as “economic sabotage”** as defined in the Act.  
The Act also states that the **maximum penalty** (the longest term and highest fine) is imposed **when the person who was illegally recruited is under 18 years old** or when the illegal recruitment was **committed by a non‑licensee or a non‑holder of authority**.  

Sources:  
- RA 8042, Section 7(a) and (b) – life imprisonment for economic sabotage.  
- RA 8042, Section 7(b) and the “Provided, however” clause – maximum penalty for minors or non‑licensed offenders.
